notes: Solved independently: the two attractions on one particle are each GM²/l² and are 60° apart, so the resultant toward the centroid is 2(GM²/l²)cos30° = √3 GM²/l². The circumradius of an equilateral triangle of side l is l/√3, so √3 GM²/l² = Mv²/(l/√3) gives v² = GM/l and v = √(GM/l), option 3. Verified with sympy. The resultant rule quoted in why_this_step, 2F cos(θ/2), is correct for two equal vectors at angle θ. Both common_mistakes entries were reproduced numerically: taking F = 2GM²/l² with r = l gives √(2GM/l) (option 1), and using only one force's component toward the centroid halves the net force and gives √(GM/2l) (option 2).
